name: Hemoglobin E-beta-thalassemia syndrome

criteria.description: Identification of compound heterozygosity for hemoglobin E mutation and beta-thalassemia mutation by molecular genetic testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis showing elevated Hb E and reduced Hb A with variable Hb F levels
Presence of chronic hemolytic anemia with variable severity and splenomegaly
Family history consistent with thalassemia or hemoglobin E trait

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Molecular genetic confirmation of compound heterozygosity plus hemoglobin electrophoresis consistent with Hb E-beta-thalassemia and clinical evidence of chronic hemolytic anemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may require differentiation from other hemoglobinopathies and thalassemias.

laboratory: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with target cells on peripheral smear
Elevated Hb E and Hb F with reduced or absent Hb A on hemoglobin electrophoresis
Elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation in iron overload
imaging: Bone deformities and marrow expansion on X-ray
Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound
other: Signs of iron overload complications such as endocrine dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or near-normal hemoglobin A levels

redFlags: Signs of iron overload such as cardiac or endocrine dysfunction
Neurological symptoms suggestive of stroke or spinal cord compression
references: Hoffman R et al. Hematology: Basic Principles and Practice. 7th edition. 2018.
Cao A, Galanello R. Beta-thalassemia. Genet Med. 2010;12(2):61-76.
